Background (from the session that started this one):
neatHack (neatlogs hackathon, ends Mon Oct 12 11:55 PM IST) entry Suture: a Python agent that takes a failing agent (Clerk, deployed on Render), proves the failure with the outside StressProof service, gets a fix, tests it, re-proves with a second signed StressProof run, keeps the fix only if score rises and quiet failures are 0, and ends with a PR for a person. Judged 30 percent agent, 25 percent use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, 20 percent demo video, 15 percent building in public, 10 percent originality. neatlogs Fixes now works: Investigate in the chats tab raised an incident, neatlogs wrote the first fix; Suture refused it (83, one quiet failure left). GitHub is connected to the project (neatlogs fixed their callback bug). The founder is non-technical, wants short plain replies and every neatlogs capability used.

Task:
You own ALL neatlogs work for the Suture neatHack entry, in C:\Users\DELL\suture (repo github.com/Sireadell/suture, public; keys are in the gitignored .env, never print or commit them). STANDING RULE from the founder: use neatlogs capabilities at every level, never add an outside tool for a job a neatlogs tool can do, never ask permission to use a sponsor tool, if a neatlogs tool falls short say exactly how and log it. Do these in order and keep each result as evidence under evidence/ (small dated commits, plain messages that say what changed, no AI or process wording, no Co-Authored-By, explicit file paths in git add, git pull --rebase before push, never touch files under evidence/entire/ which another session owns):
1. SECOND FIX ROUND. Read evidence/neatlogs_fix_attempt_1_clerk.json: the fix neatlogs wrote (incident f7b8c3b3 in app.neatlogs.com, Clerk unknown order ids) scored 83 PARTIAL with silentWrongCount 1, because malformed JSON still gets answered 200. In the neatlogs dashboard (Chrome tools; tabs hang, open fresh ones, close them after) open the chats tab (Investigate) and run an investigation on the Clerk malformed-request bug, then use the incident's Fix in, Open in Claude Code. The fix is applied on the candidate worktree C:\Users\DELL\suture\work\repo (branch suture-candidate, deploys to https://suture-clerk-candidate.onrender.com; first apply the committed first fix a88cdde, already on that branch), run targets/clerk tests with .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest, push with --force origin suture-candidate, wait for the redeploy (poll the URL), replay, then run StressProof via suture.stressproof.certify(url). Accept only if score rises AND silentWrongCount is 0; save evidence/neatlogs_fix_attempt_2_clerk.json and update evidence/scorecard.json to say the fix was written by neatlogs and proven by Suture (fields neatlogs_fixes, attempts, before/after, links).
2. EVALS. Use neatlogs evaluators/evals (neatlogs evaluators, neatlogs evals; docs https://docs.neatlogs.com, llms index https://docs.neatlogs.com/llms.txt; read the docs fully, not summaries) to score Clerk answers before and after the fix: the checklist asks for 'two neatlogs traces with the numbers compared'. Record numbers and trace ids in evidence/neatlogs_before_after.md.
3. SHARE LINKS. Create public/shareable trace or session links in neatlogs (sharing, guest links) for one before trace and one after trace; record links in evidence/neatlogs_before_after.md. No private data in them.
4. CLAUDE CODE PLUGIN. Install the neatlogs Claude Code plugin (https://docs.neatlogs.com/integrations/claude-code) so our build sessions are captured as traces; confirm a session trace appears.
5. ALERTS. Create a neatlogs alert on the 'Clerk wrong answer' detection (CLI neatlogs alerts, or dashboard). Also try Session Replay and Comments on one trace and note whether they work.
6. COMPLAINTS. Keep evidence/NEATLOGS_COMPLAINTS.md: every neatlogs bug or gap with exact reproduction, e.g. (a) MCP triage_list returns 0 while the dashboard shows the incident; (b) docs target neatlogs-cli 0.2.1, npm latest is 0.2.0 with no incidents command; (c) docs say Claude Code workers are planned but the UI offers Open in Claude Code (it is a hand-off, no PR); (d) CLI login read-only so no verdict write-back; (e) cost reads 0 and leaves out thinking tokens; (f) GitHub app callback redirect_uri error, now fixed by neatlogs. Add new ones you find.
Report back concisely: what you did, results with numbers, links, and anything blocked. Do not touch hackathon.md, README.md or suture/loop.py (planning session owns them) except where asked above.

I can't reproduce the full index verbatim because it runs to several hundred entries. Here is a condensed map of the sections, with the main hub URLs and paraphrased descriptions.

**Neatlogs** is an observability platform for AI agents and LLMs, covering traces, evals, detections, and fixes.

**Docs**
- **Welcome and quickstart:** https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs. Setup basics, including a setup wizard, a dashboard tour, and importing traces from other platforms.
- **Features:** https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs/features. Traces, session replay, comments, detections, AI-assisted investigation, tool and MCP connections, analytics, suggested fixes, experiments, evals (human and AI), alerts, and integrations.
- **FAQ:** https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs/faq. Common questions and troubleshooting.

**Guides** (https://docs.neatlogs.com/guides). Recipes for tracing RAG pipelines, LangGraph and CrewAI multi-agent setups, custom orchestration, chatbot sessions, long-running sessions, and MCP integration.

**SDKs** (https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk). Python, TypeScript, Go, a diagnostic tool, browser, plain HTTP, and OpenTelemetry options, plus guides on sessions, tags, PII redaction, span kinds, and related configuration.

**Integrations** (https://docs.neatlogs.com/integrations). Tracing support for major model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenRouter) and frameworks and agent tools (LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra, Vercel AI SDK, Pydantic AI, DSPy, Agno, Strands, Google ADK, the OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, and coding-agent plugins).

**Public API** (https://docs.neatlogs.com/api-reference). Endpoints for reading project data and automating workflows, covering authentication, pagination, errors, retries, and per-area operations such as traces, detections, evaluations, prompts, sessions, webhooks, and organizations.

**CLI** (https://docs.neatlogs.com/cli). A command-line tool with workflow guides, automation and configuration docs, and a reference page for each command group.

**Agent Skills** (https://github.com/neatlogs/skills/tree/main/skills). Packaged skills for SDK instrumentation in Python, TypeScript, and Go, direct ingest, and Public API and CLI operations. The latest skill menu is at https://github.com/neatlogs/skills/releases/latest/download/skill-menu.json.

**Full documentation bundle:** https://docs.neatlogs.com/llms-full.txt, which contains the full page content in one file.
